headline: Majors hold their 200-day lines while the crowd feels greedy and the whales quietly move coin to exchanges
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the cleanest split in this dataset. Five of the seven assets here, BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB, sit above their 200-day moving averages with golden crosses confirmed. DOGE and ADA sit below theirs with no golden cross. That's not a market in one piece: it's a market where the large-caps have repaired their long-term trend and the smaller-cap names on this board haven't. Worth noting too that even the winners are a long way from home: BTC is 38.3% off its 12-month high of $124,739.81, ETH is 47.2% off its high, SOL 59.2% off. Above the 200-day is a floor, not a victory lap.

Momentum is where it gets interesting, because it disagrees with the price action on the day. BTC is down 1.6% today and down 3.6% on the week, yet RSI-14 sits at 52.8, dead center, and MACD has just slipped below signal. That's a market cooling off from a strength move (BTC is still up 21.2% on the month) rather than a market breaking down. ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB show the same pattern: mid-50s RSI, MACD below signal, red days sitting on top of green months. Momentum is resting, not reversing, at least by what these numbers show. DOGE is the exception with RSI at 48.8 and price already under its 200-day, a genuinely weaker picture, and ADA at RSI 50.2 is treading water below trend too.

Positioning adds some texture worth flagging. BTC funding on OKX is running at 9.5% annualized, a positive but not extreme cost for longs to pay, with a long/short ratio of 1.75 and open interest at $2.2 billion. The liquidation window (6 hours, 100 events) shows longs eating $1.16 million in losses against just $8,539 for shorts, a lopsided flush that lines up with the day's red print. SOL stands apart with funding at -9.4% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs to hold their position there, a rare and specific data point on this board. XRP funding is positive at 8.8% annualized but its liquidation window shows shorts taking the bigger hit ($439,934 versus $159,988 for longs), so positioning stress is not uniform across assets even when the price moves look similar.

Flows are where the day's real tension sits. BTC spot ETFs posted a $159.9 million inflow on 14 Sep 2026, but the five-session net is a $302.8 million outflow, and same_direction_days of 1 means that single green day breaks a run of red ones rather than confirms a new trend. ETH ETFs tell a cleaner story: $121.1 million in on 14 Sep, and the five-session net is a $318.0 million inflow, a picture that agrees across both windows. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $174.2 million net onto exchanges in the last 24 hours, with ETH accounting for $125.99 million of that and BTC $76.87 million, both flagged as net onto exchanges. The weekly figures make this look less like a one-day blip: every one of the last four weeks tracked here, from the week ending Aug 25 through the week ending Sep 15, shows net flow onto exchanges, most recently $817 million for the week ending Sep 15. Coin moving toward exchanges is usually read as coin positioning to be sold or otherwise put to use, and it's happening while ETF desks are net buying ETH and, on the latest print, BTC too. Stablecoin float, the market's dry powder, is up 1.36% over 30 days to $310.3 billion, a mild build rather than a surge.

Sentiment is the foil here and it's an obvious one. The Fear & Greed gauge reads 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 31 to 74. That's a crowd feeling good about a tape that, on the numbers above, is cooling in momentum, mixed in its ETF flows, and seeing whale coin move toward exchanges on a multi-week basis. Total market cap is down 3.19% on the day to $2.65 trillion and BTC dominance sits at 58.2%, so the greed reading isn't being generated by a market that's actually ripping today.

What's worth watching from here: whether BTC's five-session ETF flow turns positive (right now it's a $302.8 million net outflow despite yesterday's single inflow), whether the weekly whale exchange flow breaks its current onto-exchanges streak, and whether SOL's negative funding (-9.4% annualized) flips positive, which would signal longs paying up again rather than shorts footing the bill. A reclaim of the 200-day by DOGE or ADA would also mark a real change in how many assets share the same regime.
